column1:
Incorporating the Beige Book alongside the FOMC statement, SLOOS, and the Financial Stability Report keeps the overall tone “moderately positive but guarded.” The Beige Book around this meeting corroborates modest-to-moderate growth across most districts, continued job gains amid tight labor supply, and generally modest-to-moderate wage and price increases—consistent with the statement’s strong labor market and ongoing business investment. At the same time, the Beige Book adds caution: rising input costs (notably materials and transportation), reports of tariff-related uncertainty, capacity and labor constraints, and mixed consumer spending in some districts. These nuances align with SLOOS’s differentiation (easier for C&I but tighter for CRE and some consumer credit) and the FSR’s elevated valuation pressures and higher nonfinancial business leverage. Netting these, the Beige Book tilts the assessment slightly more cautious than a macro-only read.
